Filter SUS health data by ICD-10 codes or disease groups with multilingual support

Source: R/sus_data_filter_cid.R
sus_data_filter_cid.Rd

Filters Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS) data based on ICD-10 codes. (International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision) or predefined epidemiological disease groups. This function supports complex filtering scenarios including specific codes, code ranges, chapters, and 50+ disease groups relevant to epidemiological research in Brazil. Includes specialized support for SUS-specific coding practices and multilingual interface (English, Portuguese, Spanish).

Usage

sus_data_filter_cid(
  df,
  icd_codes = NULL,
  disease_group = NULL,
  icd_column = NULL,
  match_type = "starts_with",
  backend = "arrow",
  lang = "pt",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

df

A climasus_df (stage "stand" or later, see sus_data_standardize()), tibble/data frame, or lazy Arrow/DuckDB table with at least one ICD-10 column. Systems without ICD-10 (SINAN, CNES, and SINASC in practice) have no auto-detectable column; pass icd_column explicitly or the function aborts with "ICD column not found".

icd_codes

Character vector of ICD-10 codes, or NULL (default). Provide either icd_codes or disease_group; if both are given, disease_group wins and icd_codes is ignored with a warning; if neither, the function aborts. Accepted forms:

  • Single or multiple codes: "J18", c("I10", "I11", "I21"). Codes are compared as written (DATASUS stores them without the dot, e.g. "J189"; use 3-character categories or prefixes such as "J18" with match_type = "starts_with").

  • Letter-number ranges: "J00-J99", "J09-J18", "C00-D48", "V01-Y98"; ranges may span several letters and are expanded to 3-character categories (e.g. J09, J10, ..., J18).

  • A single letter for a whole chapter: "I" (all I... codes, with match_type = "starts_with").

disease_group

Character scalar or vector with names of predefined disease groups, or NULL (default). Examples: "dengue", "malaria", "respiratory", "cardiovascular", "diarrheal", "heat_related", "climate_sensitive_all", "pediatric_respiratory", c("dengue", "chikungunya") (union of codes). There are 58 groups (defined in the internal .icd_disease_groups list; inspect them with names(climasus4r:::.icd_disease_groups)). Unknown names abort and list suggestions. Takes precedence over icd_codes.

icd_column

Character scalar, name of the column with ICD-10 codes, e.g. "causa_basica". NULL (default) auto-detects it from the system and lang (column names depend on lang used in sus_data_standardize()): SIM causa_basica / underlying_cause / causa_basica then the cause lines; SIH diagnostico_principal / primary_diagnosis and secondary diagnoses; SIA cid_principal / primary_icd; otherwise any column matching known ICD names.

match_type

Character scalar, how codes are matched:

  • "starts_with" (default): the column value begins with any code ("I10" matches "I10", "I100", "I109").

  • "exact": the value equals one of the codes.

  • "range": unanchored regex match of the (expanded) codes anywhere in the value. Any other value (including "chapter" and "fuzzy") is not implemented: a warning is issued and "starts_with" is used.

backend

Character scalar, "arrow" (default) or "tibble". "arrow" filters lazily and falls back to "tibble" (in memory) with a warning if it fails; "tibble" processes in memory.

lang

Character scalar, "pt" (default), "en" or "es". Language of messages and of the standardized column names looked up for ICD auto-detection.

verbose

Logical scalar, default TRUE. Print records before/after and percentage retained.

Value

The input rows whose ICD column matches, all columns preserved (a climasus_df; lazy if the input was lazy and arrow succeeded). sus_meta: stage = "filter_cid", type = "filter_cid", with a history entry describing the filter.

Details

Pipeline position: after sus_data_standardize(); next sus_data_filter_demographics() and sus_data_create_variables().

Disease groups

The predefined groups cover ICD chapters, climate-sensitive diseases (vector-borne, waterborne, heat/cold related), specific conditions (dengue, malaria, cardiovascular, respiratory, ...), syndromic groups and age-specific groups. Each group stores ICD code ranges, multilingual labels and a climate-sensitivity flag.

References

  1. World Health Organization. (2016). ICD-10 International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems. 10th Revision.

  2. Brazilian Ministry of Health. (2023). Classificacao Estatistica Internacional de Doencas e Problemas Relacionados a Saude - CID-10. DATASUS. http://datasus.saude.gov.br/cid10

See also

sus_data_standardize(), sus_data_filter_demographics(), sus_data_create_variables(), sus_data_cid_select()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example 1: Filter by explicit ICD codes
df_cardio <- sus_data_filter_cid(
  sim_data,
  icd_codes = "I00-I99",
  lang = "en"
)

# Example 2: Filter by disease group (easier!)
df_dengue <- sus_data_filter_cid(
  sinan_data,
  disease_group = "dengue",
  lang = "pt"
)

# Example 3: Climate-sensitive diseases
df_climate <- sus_data_filter_cid(
  sim_data,
  disease_group = "climate_sensitive_all",
  lang = "en"
)

# Example 4: Multiple specific codes
df_ami_stroke <- sus_data_filter_cid(
  sih_data,
  icd_codes = c("I21", "I22", "I63", "I64"),
  lang = "es"
)

# Example 5: Respiratory diseases in children
df_pediatric <- sus_data_filter_cid(
  sih_data,
  disease_group = "pediatric_respiratory",
  lang = "pt"
)

} # }
